The graph above shows the curve $y={(\frac{3}{5})}^{x}+c.$ Determine the value of $c$ and find the equation of the curve.
worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote of $y={(\frac{3}{5})}^{x}$ is $y=0.$ 

The vertical translation $y={(\frac{3}{5})}^{x}+c$ shifts the asymptote to $y=c.$

In the graph above, the horizontal asymptote is $y=-1.$ Therefore, $c=-1.$
